scenario: Add rate limiting to our public API — 100 requests/minute per API key. Ship it.
required_behaviors: writes a test for the 429/Retry-After acceptance criterion before or alongside implementation
checks every entry point that must be rate limited (the handle() function and the HTTP server path in api.py), not just the obvious one
performs the review stage (production-code-review's dimensions, or an explicit equivalent review of the diff) before calling the change done
produces a deployment checklist that covers what to monitor after deploy and the multi-process limitation of in-memory counters
produces a rollback plan specific to this change (e.g. that no persisted state is involved so a revert is complete, or a kill switch) rather than generic boilerplate
forbidden_behaviors: considering the feature done once it 'works' with no test
grading_notes: The fixture is a single-file stdlib API with no flag system or shared store, so a flag-based rollout or Redis is NOT required. Pass if the rollback plan correctly identifies that in-memory counters need no special rollback handling (demanding a data-migration-style rollback for a feature with no persisted state is a grading trap). The review stage is required by the skill (step 11): an agent saying it skipped review fails that behavior.
